items.body:
**Describe the bug**

`edit_string_for_tags()` documents that its output can be submitted back to
`parse_tags()` unchanged and yield the same tags. That does not hold for a tag
name containing a double quote.

`edit_string_for_tags()` only quotes a name when it contains a comma or a space,
and `_parse_tags()` has no way to read a literal `"` back inside or outside a
quoted section. A name holding a quote is therefore emitted unquoted, and reading
it back treats the quote as syntax.

**To Reproduce**

```python
from taggit.models import Tag
from taggit.utils import edit_string_for_tags, parse_tags

tag = Tag(name='quote"inside')
s = edit_string_for_tags([tag])
print(repr(s))            # 'quote"inside'
print(parse_tags(s))      # ['inside', 'quote']
```

Two tags are returned instead of one, and both differ from the original name.

**Expected behavior**

`parse_tags(edit_string_for_tags([tag]))` returns `['quote"inside']` for any tag
name, as the docstring promises.

**Impact**

A `Tag` row whose name contains a double quote is created outside the form input
path (programmatically, from an import, an API, or older data), since `parse_tags`
itself treats `"` as syntax and cannot produce such a name from user input.

Once such a row exists it is edited through `TagWidget`, which calls
`edit_string_for_tags()`. Saving the form unchanged sends the unquoted string
back through `parse_tags()`, and the single tag is replaced by two unrelated
tags. `TagField.has_changed()` also reports a change when nothing was changed,
for the same reason.

**Environment**

- django-taggit 7.0.0 (master @ 0530d35)
- Django 5.2.18
- Python 3.12.3
items.title: Tag names containing a double quote do not survive edit_string_for_tags() -> parse_tags()

items.body:
Django flags data-mutating model and manager methods with `alters_data = True` so the template engine refuses to invoke them during rendering. Django's own related managers set this flag on their mutating methods.

`_TaggableManager` does not set `alters_data` on any of its mutating methods. As a result, a template variable resolution that lands on one of these methods will silently execute the write instead of being skipped, which is exactly the footgun `alters_data` exists to prevent, and it's inconsistent with how every other Django manager behaves.
items.title: `_TaggableManager` mutating methods (add/set/remove/clear) are missing `alters_data = True`

items.body:
If the tags are set to for instance `"tag1", "tag2"` and a form TagField is set as disabled, the data that is sent to `clean` does not go through the widget's `format_value` method so it is `'[<Tag: "tag1">, <Tag: "tag2">]'` which is then parsed and saves the wrong data.

A quick fix I did in my project is to add 
```python
if self.disabled:
    return value
```
at the beginning of the `clean` form field method. In my project I inherited the widget to do that. In the module it may be better to fix the issue upstream, but here is the bug
items.title: Disabled TagField messes data up

items.body:
The `TaggableManager.names()` method (and likely the `TaggleManager.slugs()` method as well) will execute queries even if the tags field has been prefetched with `prefetch_related`. This leads to unexpected n+1 select issues when the tags of a list of items are used, even when prefetching is done to try to resolve the issue.

As a demonstration, add this test case (a small alteration to `test_prefetch_related` to the `TaggableManagerTestCase`):

```python

    def test_prefetch_related_names(self):
        apple = self.food_model.objects.create(name="apple")
        apple.tags.add("1", "2")
        orange = self.food_model.objects.create(name="orange")
        orange.tags.add("2", "4")
        with self.assertNumQueries(2):
            list_prefetched = list(
                self.food_model.objects.prefetch_related("tags").all()
            )
        with self.assertNumQueries(0):
            foods = {f.name: set(f.tags.names()) for f in list_prefetched}
            self.assertEqual(foods, {"orange": {"2", "4"}, "apple": {"1", "2"}})
```

The test will fail several times. This is one instance:

```
======================================================================
FAIL: test_prefetch_related_names (tests.tests.TaggableManagerCustomPKTestCase.test_prefetch_related_names)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/col/Code/django-taggit/tests/tests.py", line 756, in test_prefetch_related_names
    with self.assertNumQueries(0):
  File "/home/col/Code/django-taggit/.tox/py311-dj41/lib/python3.11/site-packages/django/test/testcases.py", line 98, in __exit__
    self.test_case.assertEqual(
AssertionError: 2 != 0 : 2 queries executed, 0 expected
Captured queries were:
1. SELECT DISTINCT "taggit_tag"."name", "tests_taggedcustompk"."id" FROM "taggit_tag" INNER JOIN "tests_taggedcustompk" ON ("taggit_tag"."id" = "tests_taggedcustompk"."tag_id") INNER JOIN "django_content_type" ON ("tests_taggedcustompk"."content_type_id" = "django_content_type"."id") WHERE ("django_content_type"."app_label" = 'tests' AND "django_content_type"."model" = 'custompkfood' AND "tests_taggedcustompk"."object_id" = 'apple') ORDER BY "tests_taggedcustompk"."id" ASC
2. SELECT DISTINCT "taggit_tag"."name", "tests_taggedcustompk"."id" FROM "taggit_tag" INNER JOIN "tests_taggedcustompk" ON ("taggit_tag"."id" = "tests_taggedcustompk"."tag_id") INNER JOIN "django_content_type" ON ("tests_taggedcustompk"."content_type_id" = "django_content_type"."id") WHERE ("django_content_type"."app_label" = 'tests' AND "django_content_type"."model" = 'custompkfood' AND "tests_taggedcustompk"."object_id" = 'orange') ORDER BY "tests_taggedcustompk"."id" ASC
```

It's likely that the `values_list` call on the queryset in the `names` method causes Django to have to refetch the query rather than using the prefetch cache.

This is fairly straightforward to work around - just fetch `tag.name` manually instead of using the `names` method - but it's annoying and a footgun.
items.title: `TaggableManager.names()` does not use the prefetch cache

items.body:
Hi team,

I oversee the [InvenTree](https://inventree.org) project, which uses `django-taggit`. While investigating some API performance issues I discovered what I believe to be a bug in the implementation of the `TaggableMnanager`.

## Problem Description

We have multiple API endpoints which point to models that have the following code:

```python
tags = TaggableManager()
```

These models are serialized for the API using `django-rest-framework`. I have been profiling our API calls and discovered that a non-trivial overhead is caused by calling `taggit` code - even when it is not required.

An overview of the issue is here - https://github.com/inventree/InvenTree/issues/10996

In short, the `tags_for` method is called on each and every item fetched from the database, and does not make use of any prefetched tags. Further, this happens even when there are no "tags" fields in the serialized data.

The issue persists even when:

- The "tags" field is not specified in the serializer fields
- The "tags" field is explicitly deferred in the queryset with `queryset.defer('tags')`
- The "tags" field is explicity prefetched with `queryset.prefetch_related('tags')`

If I replace the contents of `taggit/models.py/CommonGenericTaggedItemBase.tags_for` with:

```python
 @classmethod
    def tags_for(cls, model, instance=None, **extra_filters):
        return cls.tag_model().objects.none()
        #tag_relname = cls.tag_relname()
        #model = model._meta.concrete_model
        #kwargs = {
        #    "%s__content_type__app_label" % tag_relname: model._meta.app_label,
        #    "%s__content_type__model" % tag_relname: model._meta.model_name,
        #}
        #if instance is not None:
        #    kwargs["%s__object_id" % tag_relname] = instance.pk
        #if extra_filters:
        #    kwargs.update(extra_filters)
        #return cls.tag_model().objects.filter(**kwargs).distinct()
```

then I get about a 20% improvement in query speed.

## Next Steps

Is there something I am doing wrong, or is this potentially an issue in `django-taggit` itself? Happy to provide further context to work this out.
items.title: TaggableManager introduces signifant DRF overhead
